title: Power Automate: desktop flow libraries of reusable subflows
summary: The roadmap dates and scope match, and fresh searches did not find a library-specific availability control. However, the licensing model is reported as wholly unpublished even though Microsoft's product licensing page covers desktop authoring under Power Automate Premium; the briefing must distinguish that published entitlement from unpublished library-specific terms. Three background claims also need their supporting Microsoft sources added.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; summary; Cost and licensing; Scope; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown because Microsoft has not published which licence covers desktop flow libraries.
claims.quote: With a Power Automate Premium user license, users gain the full set of capabilities for cloud and desktop automation including premium connectors, process and task mining, AI Builder, use of managed environments, and Microsoft Dataverse storage.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included. Replace the blanket unpublished-licensing statements in the notes, summary, Cost and licensing, Scope and cost rationale with: 'Microsoft lists Power Automate Premium as providing the full set of desktop authoring capabilities. Library-specific licensing terms are not yet published.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/power-automate-licensing/overview. Do not claim Premium is the only entitlement or that libraries are free.
